source_text: His ita negotiis librorum meorum operam destinatam, mali naturalis assertor oppugnat; quibus sane viribus, et quam consequenti responsione, satis superque praecedentium voluminum disputatione perdocui. Quorum lectione non dubito prudenti cuique constare (quem rarum esse hac praefatione testatus sum), nihil studere aliud veritatis inimicum, quam ut simpliciorum ludificentur aures et evasisse, si utcumque se respondisse videatur.
pass_a_gloss: The asserter of natural evil attacks the work of my books destined for these businesses; by what powers indeed, and by how consequent a reply, I have taught more than enough by the disputation of the preceding volumes. By the reading of which I do not doubt it stands for every prudent person (whom I have testified by this preface to be rare) that the enemy of truth studies nothing other than that the ears of the simpler be mocked and that he seem to have escaped, if he seems in any way to have replied.

lemmas.lexica: LS naturalis; Blaise malum naturale=evil as a nature
LS/Blaise natura=created constitution, not 'original sin' itself
LS malum; Blaise malum naturale vs malum voluntatis
LS opus; Blaise God's works vs devil's

pass_b_english: The defender of natural evil attacks my books’ labor devoted to these matters. With what strength and how consistent an answer he does so, I have taught more than sufficiently in the preceding volumes’ discussion. I do not doubt that reading them makes this plain to every discerning person—the sort of person I have testified in this preface is rare: truth’s enemy strives only to make sport of simpler people’s ears, and thinks he has escaped if he merely appears to have answered somehow.

choices.why: Julian's Manichaean charge: an evil that is a nature, not a will's act.
Julian's charge against Augustine: treating evil as a nature rather than as will.
Keep Julian's good-of-nature vs good-of-will contrast; do not baptize as 'grace'.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
